findings.where: Nav bar "How we rank" and "Destinations"; footer "Privacy", "Terms", "How we rank", "Report content" (phone and desktop)
findings.fault: Every nav and footer link except the email goes nowhere. "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content" all reload this same page. "Destinations" points to #destinations, but the page has no destinations section, so it goes nowhere too. They are underlined and look like working links.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to know how hostels will be ranked, or what happens to their data, taps a link and lands back where they were. On a brand whose pitch is trust and ranking on merit alone, a dead "How we rank" link reads as having nothing to show. A visitor who wants to report content has no way to do it.

findings.fault: This heading is italic, turquoise and underlined, so it looks like a link, but it is static. It is also the only heading styled this way: "Surf" and "Good for" are plain ink headings. It also uses turquoise, which the brand allows as a ground or fill, as the colour of text.
findings.who_objects: Visitors tap it expecting a page about Canggu's vibe and nothing happens. A designer would object because the same heading level carries two treatments, and the link's look is used for text that does not link.

findings.where: "Good for" tags (First-time surfers, Remote workers, … Sunsets), phone and desktop
findings.fault: These fixed facts are drawn as filled pills with a coloured edge, which is the shape of a selectable filter chip, but none of them can be selected. They come in about six colours with mismatched borders: pink, magenta, purple, amber, a coral-red and lagoon. Purple, pink and magenta are not in the palette. Amber is for rewards only, and coral is for the one main action only. The colours mean nothing and change from tag to tag.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone taps "Solo travellers" expecting to filter hostels and nothing happens. Hostel comparison sites train people to read pills like these as filters. The brand owner would object to colour that carries no meaning and to the rewards and action colours used as decoration. With the rest of the page so plain, this rainbow becomes the loudest block on it, louder than the advice.

findings.where: "Coming soon" notice block above the footer
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated crimson ground that looks like the danger colour, so it reads as an error or warning banner. The brand puts this one announcement on the ink night ground. On desktop the text stops halfway across the block and leaves a large empty red area on the right.
findings.who_objects: A visitor sees a red alert box and thinks something has broken or failed. That is the wrong impression for a calm launch note. The brand owner would object because red-orange grounds are named as Hostelworld's cue, and this block breaks the rule for the interior announcement block.

findings.where: Page heading "Best Hostels in Canggu" against the page's content
findings.fault: The heading promises a list of the best hostels, but the page has none. That listings are not live is said only in the last block, after all the guide copy. The heading is also in Title Case, but the brand voice uses sentence case.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives from search for "best hostels Canggu" scrolls the whole page expecting a ranked list and finds out only at the bottom that there is none. They feel misled. Search engines also penalise a heading that the page does not deliver.

findings.where: Body copy throughout: intro, Surf, Vibe, What to look for, the notice block; worst on the phone
findings.fault: The text is fully justified. At 390 px this opens wide gaps between words ("MantaHostels    is    launching    across", "Lively  and  social"), and every paragraph has uneven, gappy lines.
findings.who_objects: A reader on a phone, the main audience, has to skip across uneven gaps, which slows reading. A typographer would object because justified text without hyphenation in a narrow column is a known fault.

findings.where: Section headings: "Surf", "Vibe", "Good for" against "WHAT TO LOOK FOR"
findings.fault: Four sections of the same rank have three heading styles. Two are plain Quicksand, one is italic, turquoise and underlined, and one is a small, widely spaced uppercase label. The section the page exists for, what to look for in a hostel, gets the weakest heading and the shortest copy.
findings.who_objects: A visitor judging which hostel to pick passes over the one practical section, because it looks like a caption while the coloured tags shout. The brief says the page should help a visitor judge what to look for, so the hierarchy runs the wrong way.

findings.fault: The text sits in a column about 520 px wide on the left, while the tags and the notice block run the full 1050 px. The right 60% of the screen beside the text is empty sand, and the blocks do not share one edge.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor sees an unfinished, lopsided page. Half the screen is empty, and the full-width blocks break the column the text sets up.

findings.where: Top of the page (first screen), phone and desktop
findings.fault: The page has no destination banner: no turquoise hero, illustration or display moment. It opens with a small grey eyebrow and a heading on plain sand. The brand says destination-page banners are its loud zone, and it names sterile as the enemy.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker deciding whether Canggu suits them gets nothing of the place's feel at first sight. The brand owner would object because the one zone meant to be loud is flat, while the loudness has moved to the tag list below.

findings.where: Notice block and end of page
findings.fault: The page ends on "listings coming soon" with no next step. There is no working link to other destinations, to how ranking will work, or anything else to do.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who came for hostels and finds none has nowhere to go but back to search. That loses them to an online travel agency on the spot.
